To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) co-evolving gene networks are associated with cancer and (b) these networks are composed of cancer genes.
The co-evolution of gene modules is a key factor in cancer development.

The co-evolution of cancer driver genes can be detected using the co-expression of genes in a gene module; the cancer driver genes in the co-evolutionary modules can be used to identify cancer driver modules that have a significant association with the cancer type; the cancer driver modules can be used as a tool to identify the cancer type of an unknown patient; the cancer driver module approach can be used to predict the response of a patient to a drug.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel approach for identifying genes and pathways that are associated with a particular disease.
the problem of identifying cancer genes by analyzing gene co-expression networks.
the problem of identifying the most significant cancer genes from the co-evolutionary gene modules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results of the current study are in line with the results of previous studies and the results of the present study are consistent with the results of the previous study.
there is no evidence to support the idea that cancer is an evolutionary process.
the gene module approach is an effective way of identifying co-evolving genes and their functions, and the gene module approach could be applied in cancer studies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are trying to find out how the cancer gene network evolves.
we developed a new method to identify co-evolving genes and modules in a network.
we are trying to understand the evolutionary history of cancer genes, and how this relates to cancer biology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can learn a great deal from the co-evolution of genes.
cancer is a disease of gene modules.
the cancer driver genes are not randomly distributed in a genome but rather tend to co-evolve in a gene module with other genes.
